title: Service Outage Coordination and Stakeholder Briefing Kit
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary

This kit centralizes procedures, templates, and checklists for coordinating a multi-team service outage at Redwood Inference. It is intended for Incident Leads, Communication Leads, SRE responders, Customer Success, and Product managers who must rapidly align external and internal communications while preserving incident evidence and SLO context.

Purpose

- Provide a single source of truth for: incident coordination timeline, stakeholder briefings, external status updates, and post-incident handoff.
- Reduce variance between incidents so that customers and executives receive clear, consistent, and timely information.

Scope

Applies to all incidents that meet Severity S0–S2 (see definitions below). Minor operational items (S3) should still use the internal incident-to-task flow but do not normally require external comms unless customer impact is observed.

Key Principles

1. Fast alignment over perfect detail: publish an initial external status within 15 minutes for S0/S1/S2 incidents.
2. Single source of truth: the Incident Lead owns the incident timeline and status page copy.
3. Clear ownership of comms: Communication Lead drafts external messages; Customer Success reviews for customer-specific impacts.

Incident coordination workflow (high level)

1) Detection & Triage (0–5 minutes)
   - Pager/alert to on-call responder.
   - On-call responder confirms reproducibility and initial impact.
   - If confirmed and impact >= S2, escalate to Incident Lead.

2) Mobilize (5–15 minutes)
   - Incident Lead declares incident, assigns roles (Incident Lead, Comm Lead, Primary Responder, Secondary Responder, Scribe).
   - Create incident run channel (Slack #incident-<service>-YYYYMMDD-001).
   - Open incident doc in the incident tracker (link template provided in Appendix).

3) Notify & Publish Initial Status (<=15 minutes for S0–S2)
   - Comm Lead prepares initial status using the template below and posts to status.redwood.ai and customer-facing channels.
   - Internal all-hands notification to execs and product-owner mailing list.

4) Contain & Mitigate (15–90 minutes)
   - Run troubleshooting playbooks.
   - Execute mitigations (rollbacks, routing changes, capacity surge) as approved by Incident Lead.
   - Log actions in timeline with timestamps and owners.

5) Recovery & Verification (90–240 minutes)
   - Validate service health and SLO metrics for 15–30 minutes before declaring recovery.
   - Comm Lead updates status with mitigation steps and ETA for postmortem.

6) Close & Postmortem (within 72 hours)
   - Incident Lead files a post-incident summary.
   - Postmortem reviewers assigned; learnings scheduled into the roadmap or runbook backlog.

Roles & responsibilities

- Incident Lead (usually senior SRE or service owner)
  - Declares incident severity and timeline, approves external messages, coordinates escalations.

- Communication Lead (SRE + Customer Success rotation)
  - Drafts and publishes status page updates, customer emails, and exec briefs.

- Primary Responder(s)
  - Executes technical mitigations and documents commands/actions.

- Secondary Responder
  - Shadow and pick up tasks or take over if primary becomes unavailable.

- Scribe
  - Maintains the incident timeline, captures logs, and preserves evidence for postmortem.

Severity definitions & SLO impact

- S0: Complete outage impacting all customers or critical internal systems; targeted human response immediately.
- S1: Major degradation affecting a subset of customers or some critical functionality; high priority.
- S2: Partial degradation with increased error rates/latency but workarounds exist; requires attention.
- S3: Functional degradation with limited or no customer impact; tracked as an engineering ticket.

Table: quick reference (as plain text)

Severity | Typical symptoms | Initial comms required | SLA impact threshold
S0 | 100% errors or unavailable | Status page + email + outreach | Major SLA breach, exec notified
S1 | Large fraction customers affected | Status page + scheduled updates | Potential SLA exposure
S2 | Partial errors/latency | Status page entry + internal brief | Monitor for SLA drift
S3 | Low impact | Internal ticket | No SLA impact

Immediate actions (first 15 minutes)

1. Confirm incident and severity.
2. Incident Lead: create channel and incident doc.
3. Comm Lead: draft initial status (see template).
4. Primary Responder: capture `top`/`iostat`/`nvidia-smi` and save output to incident doc.
5. Scribe: begin timeline with timestamps and owners.

External communications cadence and templates

Guidelines
- Use clear, non-technical language for customers; include technical details in an "Expanded Details" section for interested engineering contacts.
- Every external update should include: impact summary, affected services/customers, mitigation steps in-progress, ETA for next update.
- Publish updates on the status page first, then mirror to email/slack/CS signals as appropriate.

Initial status (status page) template (use plain text):

Title: Service disruption impacting <service-name>
Status: Identified
Started: <ISO timestamp>
Impact: Users may experience <description of impact>. We are investigating and will provide updates every <N> minutes.
Mitigation: Our engineers are actively investigating.
Next update: <time window, e.g., 30 minutes>

Customer email (short) template:

Subject: Incident affecting <service-name> – we are investigating

Hi <CustomerName>,

We are investigating an issue impacting <service-name> that may affect your requests. Our team is actively working on mitigation and we will share updates via https://status.redwood.ai.

We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with details and an ETA as soon as possible.

— Redwood Inference Support

Periodic update template (status page)

Status: Investigating / Mitigating / Identified
Update time: <ISO timestamp>
Summary: Short recap of progress since last update.
Actions taken: List of mitigation steps and owner initials.
Next update: <time or ‘when more info available’>

Final update template

Status: Resolved
Resolved: <ISO timestamp>
Summary: Brief explanation of root cause and remediation applied.
Customer impact: Which customers/features were affected and duration.
Follow-up: Postmortem will be published to <link> within <X> business days.

Internal briefing: executive one-pager (30–60 lines max)

- Incident ID: INC-<service>-YYYYMMDD-xxx
- Severity: S0|S1|S2
- Start/End times: <ISO> / <ISO or ongoing>
- Impact summary: concise sentence(s) describing customer/business impact
- Root cause hypothesis: short bullet(s)
- Actions taken: top 3 mitigations and outcomes
- Customer outreach: who was contacted and when
- Next steps: postmortem owner and ETA, compensation evaluation if applicable

Post-incident handoff checklist (prior to closing ticket)

1. Ensure system metrics are stable for 30 minutes (error rate and latency).
2. Archive logs and attach to incident doc (retention policy note: preserve logs for 90 days).
3. Identify action items and owners; create tickets with priority and due dates.
4. Schedule postmortem review session within 72 hours.

Game day & rotation tie-ins

- Quarterly game days will exercise the coordination flow in this kit; rotation teams should use the exact templates and timing windows to validate SLAs and comms latency.
- New on-call hires must shadow two incidents and run one tabletop exercise before independent rotation.

Appendix B: sample status page JSON payload (example for engineering use only)

{
  "incident_id": "INC-service-20260120-001",
  "status": "identified",
  "started_at": "2026-01-20T10:12:00Z",
  "summary": "Service generation requests are returning 5xx errors for some regions.",
  "updates": [
    {"at": "2026-01-20T10:15:00Z", "message": "Investigating - engineering triage in progress"}
  ]
}

Appendix C: common troubleshooting commands (copy into incident doc)

- Kubernetes: kubectl -n <ns> get pods -o wide
- Logs: rg -n "ERROR|exception" /var/log/service/*.log | head -n 200
- GPU health: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu --format=csv

Retention & evidence handling

- All incident artifacts (timelines, logs, runbook snapshots) must be stored in the incident repo for at least 90 days.
- For incidents with customer data exposure, follow security-and-compliance/data-incident-guidance and mark the incident confidentiality as restricted.

Governance & continuous improvement

- Every S0/S1 incident triggers a mandatory postmortem review with exec presence.
- Action items from postmortems must be tracked in the engineering backlog and triaged by owners within two sprints.

How to use this kit in a live incident

1. Read the Immediate actions section and choose the correct template for comms.
2. Use the incident channel naming convention to ensure discoverability.
3. Keep messages short and time-stamped; the scribe should post the timeline to the incident doc every 15 minutes.

Document maintenance

- Owner: Incident Response Guild (eng-sre).
- Review cadence: annual or after any S0 incident.
- Suggested updates: add service-specific mitigations and contacts per-quarter.
